title: Free-representable internal Hom evaluated on product slices
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site in the common sheaf universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with finite products and subcanonical topology (every representable is a sheaf). Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and let $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ denote ordinary module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $U$ for the underlying abelian sheaf functor, $\iota$ for inclusion of abelian sheaves into presheaves, and $a$ for abelian sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. For $P\in\mathcal C$ put $F_P(W)=\bigoplus_{b:W\to P}R(W)$ with restriction $e_b\mapsto e_{b\circ d}$ along $d:W'\to W$, and $R[P]=F_P^\#$, using module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. For $V\in\mathcal C$ restriction is to the site $\mathcal C/V$ of arrows to $V$, with underlying coverings [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Then $R[P]|_V$ is canonically the module sheafification of the free $R|_V$-module presheaf on $(V\times P\to V)$; at $(W\xrightarrow{b_0}V)$ its generator indexed by $b:W\to P$ corresponds to $e_{(b_0,b)}$.
Put $H_P(M)=\mathcal Hom_R(R[P],M)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom] and $(t_PA)(V)=A(V\times P)$ for abelian presheaves $A$. There is an additive isomorphism of abelian presheaves
$$\theta_{P,M}:\iota UH_P(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}t_P\iota UM.$$
Its value at $V$ sends $\varphi:R[P]|_V\to M|_V$ to $\varphi_{(V\times P\to V)}(e_{\operatorname{pr}_P})$; the inverse sends $s\in M(V\times P)$ to the map taking $e_b$ over $(W\xrightarrow{b_0}V)$ to $s|_{(b_0,b)}$. It commutes with restriction along $c:V'\to V$ via $c\times1_P$, with a coefficient map $f:M\to N$ via $f_{V\times P}$, and with $u:P'\to P$ via restriction along $1_V\times u$ (the Hom map is precomposition by $R[u]$). The additive functor $H_P$ is left exact. Applying $a$ and the counit $a\iota\cong\mathrm{id}$ yields $\bar\theta_{P,M}:UH_P(M)\cong a t_P\iota UM$ with the same naturalities. For every cochain complex $L^\bullet$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] these maps give an isomorphism of complexes $UH_P(L^\bullet)\cong a t_P\iota UL^\bullet$, natural for chain maps and for $u$. If $L^n=0$ for $n<0$ and $r:M[0]\to L^\bullet$ identifies $M$ with $\ker d_L^0$, its restriction to the degree-zero kernels is precisely $\bar\theta_{P,M}$.

source.place: Tag 03EM (lemma-internal-hom), its localized-Hom definition and free-generator specialization; module sheafification and localization in lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules and definition-localize-ringed-site. Agent formulation with explicit inverse and naturality.

proof.text: Put $Q=(UF_P)|_{\mathcal C/V}$ and $S=a_VQ$. The site and its slice are small in the common sheaf universe, so [lem-cbc-sieve-slice-sheafification], with abelian-group values, gives $\alpha:S\cong U(R[P]|_V)$ with $\alpha\eta_Q=(\eta_{F_P})|_V$. Transport the restricted module action by $r\cdot_Sx=\alpha^{-1}(r\cdot\alpha(x))$. The unit identity gives $r\cdot_S\eta_Q(q)=\alpha^{-1}(r\cdot\alpha\eta_Q(q))=\alpha^{-1}(\alpha\eta_Q(rq))=\eta_Q(rq)$ on each object, because the original module sheafification unit is linear. Thus this action extends the presheaf action, and uniqueness in [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] identifies it with the slice module-sheafification action. For each $(W\xrightarrow{b_0}V)$, the product universal property gives the bijection $b\mapsto(b_0,b)$ from $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(W,P)$ to $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C/V}((W,b_0),(V\times P,\operatorname{pr}_V))$. Extend it linearly; precomposition by $d$ sends both generators to the one indexed by $(b_0d,bd)$. This is an isomorphism of free module presheaves. Sheafifying and composing with $\alpha$ proves the asserted slice identification with its specified generators. The coefficient ring and restrictions here are exactly those of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site].

source.place: Tags 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), 04IX (definition-localize-ringed-site); slice compatibility as stated in lem-cbc-sieve-slice-sheafification

proof.text: Fix $s\in M(V\times P)$. On the free presheaf of step 1 define $\psi_s(\sum_b r_be_b)=\sum_b r_b\,s|_{(b_0,b)}$ over $(W,b_0)$. The sums are finite and the formula is $R(W)$-linear. Along $d:W'\to W$ both restriction of this formula and application of the formula after restriction give $\sum_b r_b|_{W'}\,s|_{(b_0d,bd)}$. Thus it is a morphism of module presheaves. The module sheafification universal property extends it uniquely to $\varphi_s:R[P]|_V\to M|_V$. Uniqueness also shows $\varphi_{s+t}=\varphi_s+\varphi_t$ and $\varphi_0=0$.

source.place: Tag 03CY, factorization through module sheafification; explicit free-generator specialization of Section 04TT

proof.text: By [def-pur-sheaf-hom], a section of $H_P(M)$ at $V$ is precisely a map $\varphi:R[P]|_V\to M|_V$. Set $s=\varphi_{(V\times P,\operatorname{pr}_V)}(e_{\operatorname{pr}_P})$. Naturality of $\varphi$ along the slice arrow $(b_0,b):(W,b_0)\to(V\times P,\operatorname{pr}_V)$ says $\varphi_{(W,b_0)}(e_b)=s|_{(b_0,b)}$. Linearity and uniqueness of factorization through sheafification imply $\varphi=\varphi_s$. Conversely, evaluating $\varphi_s$ on $e_{\operatorname{pr}_P}$ gives $s|_{(\operatorname{pr}_V,\operatorname{pr}_P)}=s$. Evaluation is additive because addition of maps is sectionwise. Hence these constructions are mutually inverse additive bijections at every $V$.

source.place: Section 04TT and Tag 03EM (lemma-internal-hom), with the explicit free-generator inverse

proof.text: For $c:V'\to V$ and $s\in M(V\times P)$, restricting $\varphi_s$ to $\mathcal C/V'$ sends a generator $e_b$ over $(W,b_0':W\to V')$ to $s|_{(cb_0',b)}=(s|_{c\times1_P})|_{(b_0',b)}$. Uniqueness of sheafification extension therefore identifies it with $\varphi_{s|_{c\times1_P}}$. For $f:M\to N$, the composite $f\varphi_s$ sends $e_b$ to $f_W(s|_{(b_0,b)})=f_{V\times P}(s)|_{(b_0,b)}$. Finally define $R[u]:R[P']\to R[P]$ by sheafifying $e_{b'}\mapsto e_{ub'}$. The composite $\varphi_s R[u]|_V$ sends $e_{b'}$ to $s|_{(b_0,ub')}=(s|_{1_V\times u})|_{(b_0,b')}$. These three identities prove all three naturalities and show that the bijections of step 3 constitute the asserted presheaf isomorphism $\theta_{P,M}$.

source.place: Section 04TT, restriction by relocalization; Tag 03CY for equality after extension

proof.text: Kernels of module-sheaf morphisms are computed sectionwise by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. If $K=\ker(f:M\to N)$, then $K(V\times P)=\ker(f_{V\times P})$. Under $\theta$, the map $H_P(f)(V)$ is $f_{V\times P}$ by step 4. Thus $H_P(K)\to H_P(M)$ is its kernel, sectionwise at every $V$. Also $H_P(0)=0$, and $H_P$ is additive by composition of module maps. It preserves binary sums since pairs of maps to $M\oplus N$ are precisely a map to $M$ and a map to $N$, componentwise on every slice. Consequently $H_P$ preserves zero objects, binary products and kernels, hence finite limits, and is left exact.

source.place: Tag 03DA (lemma-abelian), sectionwise kernels; compare Tag 0GMY (lemma-internal-hom-exact), clause (2)

proof.text: Sheafify $\theta$ as an abelian-presheaf isomorphism. Since $UH_P(M)$ is already an abelian sheaf, its sheafification unit is invertible: the identity factors through the unit by the universal property, and uniqueness makes the two composites identities. Let $\epsilon:a\iota\cong\mathrm{id}$ be this counit. Define $\bar\theta_{P,M}=a(\theta_{P,M})\circ\epsilon_{UH_P(M)}^{-1}$. Naturality of sheafification and of this counit gives all three naturalities already proved in step 4. Sheafification is additive here: it preserves finite products by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact], so it preserves the addition maps induced by those products. Thus these are natural additive isomorphisms.

Apply $\bar\theta$ in each degree to $L^\bullet$. Naturality for the coefficient morphism $d_L^n:L^n\to L^{n+1}$ gives $\bar\theta_{P,L^{n+1}}\circ UH_P(d_L^n)=a(t_P\iota U(d_L^n))\circ\bar\theta_{P,L^n}$, so these maps form a cochain map. Their degreewise inverses give its inverse cochain map by the same equality. For a chain map $g:L^\bullet\to T^\bullet$, apply coefficient naturality to every $g^n$; for $u:P'\to P$, apply the parameter identity of step 4 in every degree. These are exactly the required naturalities of the complex isomorphism.

source.place: Explicit degreewise consequence of the coefficient and parameter naturalities proved above

proof.text: Let $r^0:M\to L^0$ identify $M$ with $\ker d_L^0$. Step 5 identifies $UH_P(r^0)$ with the degree-zero kernel inclusion on the left. On abelian presheaves, $t_P\iota U(r^0)$ is the kernel inclusion of $t_P\iota U(d_L^0)$, since its value at $V$ is the kernel inclusion at $V\times P$. Exactness of $a$ in [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact] identifies $a t_P\iota U(r^0)$ with the degree-zero kernel inclusion on the right. Coefficient naturality for $r^0$ reads $\bar\theta_{P,L^0}\,UH_P(r^0)=a t_P\iota U(r^0)\,\bar\theta_{P,M}$. Since the latter inclusion is monic, the map induced on the two kernels is exactly $\bar\theta_{P,M}$. The vanishing in negative degrees ensures these are also the degree-zero cohomology objects, with no boundaries to quotient out.
